files.adapted_why: Adapted for this repo; every deviation from the kit is listed in the PERMUTO ADAPTATIONS block at the top of the file: `tidy` runs against this repo's own .clang-tidy (the bug-finding subset — clang-diagnostic-* + clang-analyzer-*, 0 findings, 104-201 s; the two heavier rule sets and why they were rejected are in INCIDENTS.md), stage_version also compares the generated $CI_BUILD_DIR/*ConfigVersion.cmake (a third copy of the version number no kit stage looks at), Permuto's own defaults (CI_VERSION_BINARIES, CI_DEFAULT_STAGES) are set by plain assignment after the kit's block, and --help derives its header range from the PERMUTO ADAPTATIONS marker because the kit's first-blank-line rule would cut the local notes off. The only byte difference that is NOT a Permuto decision is a literal newline inside one printf format string in write_tidy_baseline() (output-identical; all four ports of the 2026-09-20 tidy-baseline fix carry it). The kit's tidy-baseline fix itself (tidy_key on both operands + --write-tidy-baseline) was ported in here by cbb7248, so this copy is not lagging the kit.

The stage list is the kit's own verbatim (--require-clean tree format kitprobes build tests version asan tsan tidy pristine); the only difference is the nine-line PERMUTO comment above the exec, which records what `tidy` certifies here (.clang-tidy's bug-finding subset) and where the clean-tree check lived while the `tree` stage could not pass.

Permuto's real config: CI_DEFAULT_STAGES spelled out with tidy included, CI_VERSION_BINARIES=$CI_BUILD_DIR/permuto, the note that the third version copy (the generated *ConfigVersion.cmake) deliberately has no knob, the kit's optional CI_ASAN_TEST_CMD example block absent (nothing here filters the suite under a sanitizer: `grep -rn GTEST_FILTER tests/ .ci.env.example` finds nothing, and there is no RSS-measuring or wall-clock test), and a PERMUTO NOTES section at the end recording what is wired, the rule set `tidy` runs and the two heavier rule sets rejected with their measured numbers.

Seeded from the kit's rule block (the first 15 lines are byte-identical to the kit's) and then filled with THIS repo's entries — seven at record time, including one marked SUPERSEDED. The kit's own entries are deliberately not copied, so a sync must never overwrite this file with the kit's.
